content.user_title: Improve NestJS Features, Performance, and Reliability
content.value_statement: NestJS runtime changes can create latency, security, and deployment failures when teams lack clear contracts and measurements. This skill guides component selection, bottleneck diagnosis, and reliable implementation using repository evidence and focused tests.
actual_capabilities: Guides placement of validation, authorization, timing, and error mapping in pipes, guards, interceptors, and exception filters.
Defines stable application failures and maps them independently across HTTP, GraphQL, RPC, gRPC, WebSocket, and worker boundaries.
Structures performance diagnosis around latency percentiles, event-loop delay, database queries, memory, external calls, and representative workloads.
Guides queue idempotency, bounded retries, cancellation, backpressure, cache safety, and graceful shutdown.
Provides security and testing checklists for tenant authorization, input bounds, response allow-lists, and secret redaction.
Guides immutable artifact delivery, Kubernetes probes, autoscaling, SLO-based observability, rollout verification, and recovery planning.
limitations: Targets NestJS services, not frontend-only performance or unrelated backend frameworks.
Contains guidance and evaluation scenarios, not a bundled profiler, benchmark runner, or deployment tool.
Requires repository access, installed version checks, and representative measurements to justify specific runtime changes.
Cannot guarantee performance gains or production readiness without executed tests, live evidence, and authorized environment access.

use_cases.title: Implement a Secure Endpoint
use_cases.description: Choose lifecycle components for validation, authorization, response shaping, and stable errors, then define boundary tests.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Service Latency
use_cases.description: Compare traces and resource metrics to identify a dominant bottleneck and design a repeatable optimization experiment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Reliable Release
use_cases.description: Review artifact identity, probes, migrations, worker drain, telemetry, and recovery controls before a consequential deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Choose Lifecycle Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NestJS endpoint and recommend where validation, authorization, timing, and error mapping belong. Explain binding scope and propose focused tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adding common endpoint behavior without mixing lifecycle responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Diagnose Latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Our NestJS endpoint has p95 latency of 1.8 seconds. Identify the smallest missing measurements and propose one controlled experiment with correctness checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigating a slow endpoint before selecting an optimization.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Repair Error Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review error handling for our HTTP, GraphQL, and queue entry points. Define transport-neutral failure categories, safe mappings, logging ownership, and contract tests. Preserve existing client compatibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Making failures consistent without forcing every transport into an HTTP error model.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Plan a Safe Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess a rolling Kubernetes release for our NestJS payment worker using the supplied manifests, telemetry, and job contract. Define idempotency, retry budgets, drain deadlines, success signals, and recovery steps. Do not mutate production.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a consequential deployment with explicit failure and recovery controls.

output_examples.input: An endpoint has high latency, but no traces or resource metrics are available.
output: Baseline evidence is missing. Record p95 and p99 latency, throughput, errors, workload shape, and resource saturation.
Collect one representative trace covering database queries and external calls before selecting a remedy.
Compare one targeted change under the same workload and retain correctness and failure tests.

output_examples.input: A payment provider times out, and the team proposes immediate retries.
output: Treat the payment outcome as unknown because a timeout does not prove that the charge failed.
Require provider idempotency or reconciliation before repeating a possible side effect.
Define a total deadline, bounded retry policy, cancellation support, and tests for duplicate and uncertain outcomes.

output_examples.input: NestJS Pods restart during database outages and drop requests during rollouts.
output: Verify the running image, probe configuration, events, and traffic symptoms before editing desired state.
Keep ordinary database outages out of liveness checks and use bounded readiness checks to control incoming work.
Measure shutdown drain time and align termination grace, intake stop, and resource closure with rollout behavior.

best_practices: Read repository conventions and installed versions before choosing framework APIs or deployment controls.
Measure a representative baseline and change one limiting factor before claiming an improvement.
Verify contracts, sensitive-data absence, bounded resources, shutdown behavior, and recovery paths at the appropriate test boundaries.
anti_patterns: Adding Redis, Fastify, worker threads, or service boundaries without evidence of the limiting resource.
Retrying uncertain writes without idempotency, reconciliation, classification, and a total deadline.
Treating source configuration, passing unit tests, or a successful build as proof of production safety.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The declared supported tools are Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill include executable profiling tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides Markdown guidance and evaluation scenarios. Measurements require the tools available in your repository and runtime environment.

faq.question: Can it guarantee faster endpoints?
faq.answer: No. It requires representative baseline and post-change measurements, plus correctness checks, before supporting a performance claim.

faq.question: Does it cover transports beyond HTTP?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers GraphQL, WebSockets, SSE, RPC, gRPC, message consumers, and workers with transport-specific contracts and verification.

faq.question: Is Kubernetes required?
faq.answer: No. Kubernetes and container guidance applies only when the target repository uses those deployment models.

faq.question: Does this skill authorize production changes?
faq.answer: No. Its workflow requires verified targets, explicit authorization, compatible rollout plans, and recovery controls before consequential changes.
